_notes: Does the shared doctrine (youcoded#423) change what the assistant actually does? Two builds of the SAME code, differing only in the prompt: 'before' is a12396fa (the merge before #423), 'after' is 085ef667.

Cases chosen to hit the rules that changed. config-investigation is 'find out what is wrong and report back' — the question-vs-action rule says that ends in findings, not edits, so the before/after gap should show as fewer unasked Write/Edit calls. options-proposal is 'tell me my options' — it exercises the new writing block and the rule that a final message offers two or three ways forward with a recommendation.

Models: Qwen 3.6 27B is the smallest on the roster and the same open-weight family the local path runs, so it stands in for the model with the least room for a longer prompt. Claude Opus 5 is the control: a frontier model already has these habits, so a gap there would mean the prompt is doing something unintended rather than teaching.
CAVEAT: every OpenRouter model resolves as cloud, so all four arms get the FULL doctrine. The COMPACT form a small LOCAL model gets is not measured by this run.
Instructions arm is the baseline (no project file) so the only variable is the app's own prompt.
name: prompt-doctrine
